items.subject: A collection of faded photographs showing Australian and European migrant miners from the 1960s.
items.action: Hanging on a plain wall, representing the hundreds of deceased workers.
items.gaze_interaction: The faces in the photographs look out with neutral expressions, fixed in the past.
items.setting: A quiet, commemorative room in an advocacy group's office, circa 1989.
items.color_palette: Sepia, black and white, and the faded colours of old photographs against a muted beige wall.
items.props_detail: Dozens of small, mismatched frames containing individual portraits.
items.lens_technique: Shallow depth of field, 50mm lens, focusing on a few photographs.
items.lighting: Soft, diffused daylight from an unseen window.
items.mood: Somber, silent remembrance, the scale of loss conveyed by the number of individual lives.
items.narration_anchor: En mil novecientos ochenta y nueve ya habían muerto más de quinientos antiguos trabajadores y residentes de Wittenoom.

items.subject: A group of middle-aged and older men and women, former Wittenoom residents.
items.action: Meeting in a community hall, sitting in a circle of chairs, engaged in a serious discussion.
items.gaze_interaction: Listening intently to a speaker out of frame, faces showing lines of fatigue and worry.
items.setting: A sparse community meeting room, late 1970s, with institutional furniture.
items.color_palette: Muted beige, institutional green, faded wood tones.
items.props_detail: A simple folding table holding a pitcher of water and some scattered papers.
items.mood: Quiet solidarity and shared burden, a small group facing a monumental challenge.
items.narration_anchor: Los que seguían vivos se habían juntado diez años antes en la Asbestos Diseases Society of Australia.

items.subject: An Australian judge in traditional robes, seen from a low side angle.
items.action: Reading aloud from a thick document at a high bench in a courtroom.
items.gaze_interaction: Eyes focused downward on the text of the verdict.
items.color_palette: Dark mahogany wood tones, black fabric of the robes, cream-colored paper.
items.props_detail: A thick, bound legal document spread open on the judge's bench.
items.lens_technique: 50mm lens, focusing on the judge and the document.
items.lighting: Solemn, directional light highlighting the bench, with the rest of the courtroom in shadow.
items.mood: The immense gravity of justice being delivered, a moment of formal condemnation.
items.narration_anchor: En mil novecientos ochenta y ocho un juez leyó su veredicto: la compañía había mostrado un desprecio continuo, consciente y contumaz por la seguridad y la salud de sus trabajadores.

items.subject: A middle-aged woman, appearing to be a Spanish former resident of Wittenoom.
items.action: Lying still on the sliding bed of a CT scanner as it moves her into the machine's large circular aperture.
items.gaze_interaction: Her eyes look straight up, her body is motionless, hands resting at her sides.
items.setting: A sterile hospital examination room from the late 1980s.
items.color_palette: Clinical whites, greys, and the light blue of a hospital gown.
items.props_detail: The large, beige-white cylindrical form of a late 1980s CT scanner.
items.camera_angle: Eye-level, from the side of the machine.
items.mood: Clinical impersonality, a sense of human vulnerability within the workings of medical technology.
items.narration_anchor: Mercedes de Juan, que se quedó en Australia, entra en un escáner y después sopla en un tubo.

items.subject: The same middle-aged Spanish woman from the previous scene.
items.action: Sitting upright in a hospital chair, exhaling with maximum effort into the tube of a spirometer.
items.gaze_interaction: Her cheeks are puffed and her face is taut with exertion, eyes focused on a point just beyond the camera.
items.setting: A hospital testing room with medical equipment.
items.color_palette: Clinical whites and greys, with the blue of her hospital gown.
items.props_detail: A spirometry device with a clear plastic mouthpiece and coiled tube.
items.mood: A feeling of physical strain, the invisible damage inside the body being quantified.
items.narration_anchor: «Nos hacen un escáner y una prueba de función pulmonar», dice Mercedes.

items.subject: A medical chest X-ray.
items.action: Displayed on a lightbox, the image shows the web-like scarring and pleural thickening of advanced asbestosis.
items.gaze_interaction: The focus is the texture of the damaged lung tissue.
items.color_palette: Stark black, white, and translucent greys of the X-ray film.
items.props_detail: The glowing X-ray film, showing clear evidence of fibrous lung damage.
items.lens_technique: Macro lens, capturing the fine details of the scarring.
items.lighting: The image is the sole light source, glowing intensely from the light box.
items.mood: Cold, clinical finality; the undeniable visual proof of internal destruction.
items.narration_anchor: Las fibras pueden causar mesotelioma, asbestosis y cáncer de pulmón.

items.subject: A hand holding a metal, mechanical tally counter.
items.action: The thumb stops pressing the button, and the numbered wheels freeze, halting the count.
items.gaze_interaction: The focus is on the mechanism coming to a dead stop.
items.setting: A cluttered government office desk, circa 2000.
items.color_palette: Dull metallic sheen, beige plastic, and the grey of dusty office equipment.
items.props_detail: The hand-held tally counter, its digits frozen on a number in the thousands.
items.lens_technique: Macro lens with a very shallow depth of field.
items.lighting: Harsh, focused light from a single desk lamp.
items.mood: An abrupt, bureaucratic halt; the deliberate act of ceasing to acknowledge a growing tragedy.
items.narration_anchor: La cuenta oficial se detuvo. «El gobierno dejó de contar en 2.000, pero ahora se calcula que la cifra puede ser superior a los 4.000.

items.subject: A young Australian man in his late 20s, the son of a former Wittenoom worker.
items.action: Sitting slumped on the edge of a hospital bed, his posture conveying exhaustion and defeat.
items.gaze_interaction: His head is bowed into his hands, obscuring his face completely.
items.setting: A simple, public hospital room with minimal furnishings.
items.color_palette: Pale institutional greens, whites, and the light blue of patient clothing.
items.lighting: Soft, flat light coming from a large window to one side.
items.mood: The silent weight of inherited tragedy, quiet suffering that spans generations.
items.narration_anchor: Y sigue aumentando», dice Melita Markey. Están enfermando hijos de policías y de maestros que trabajaron en el pueblo.

items.subject: The hand of a government official.
items.action: Drawing a thick, heavy red line through the town's name on an official document, striking it out.
items.gaze_interaction: The focus is on the decisive, forceful movement of the marker across the paper.
items.setting: A bureaucratic office desk cluttered with papers and files.
items.color_palette: Stark white paper, black printed text, and the aggressive, saturated red of the marker ink.
items.props_detail: A government report with 'Wittenoom' clearly typed, now being redacted.
items.mood: A cold and definitive act of bureaucratic erasure, wiping a problem off the page.
items.narration_anchor: Mientras los enfermos se contaban a sí mismos, el Estado decidió qué hacer con el pueblo: borrarlo.

items.subject: Two road workers next to a large highway sign.
items.action: Removing the metal letters that spell 'Wittenoom' from the sign, leaving a blank space.
items.gaze_interaction: Their faces are turned away or obscured as they focus on the manual task.
items.setting: A roadside in the vast, red-earthed Australian outback, circa 2007.
items.color_palette: The deep green of the road sign, metallic silver letters, against the ochre of the desert and a vast blue sky.
items.props_detail: The large, official green highway directional sign, now visibly defaced.
items.lens_technique: Wide-angle lens with deep depth of field.
items.lighting: Harsh, bright midday sun casting sharp shadows.
items.mood: A stark, physical act of erasure; the official removal of a place from public existence.
items.narration_anchor: Junio de dos mil siete; otras fuentes dicen dos mil seis. Wittenoom es abolido formalmente. Le quitan el nombre a las señales de la carretera y lo sacan de los mapas.

items.subject: A government official in a dark suit, seen from behind the shoulder.
items.action: Standing at a podium, addressing an unseen audience during a press conference.
items.gaze_interaction: The figure's head is angled towards the bank of microphones, face obscured.
items.setting: A formal press briefing room with an official state crest on the wall behind the podium.
items.color_palette: Corporate blues and dark greys of the suit, rich wood tones of the podium.
items.props_detail: A cluster of microphones on the podium, bearing logos of various news agencies.
items.lens_technique: 85mm lens, shallow depth of field focusing on the microphones.
items.lighting: Bright, direct lighting typical of a staged press event.
items.mood: Polished, disingenuous officialdom; a narrative being carefully managed and brought to a close.
items.narration_anchor: El gobierno de Australia Occidental habla de «el fin de un período oscuro en la historia de nuestro Estado».

items.subject: A thick, bound parliamentary report from 1992.
items.action: Lying on a dark wood desk, its cover stamped with a large, decisive red mark.
items.gaze_interaction: The focus is on the stamped word, signifying the dismissal of the report's contents.
items.setting: A government office interior, suggesting the 1990s.
items.color_palette: Yellowed cream paper, black serif type, and stark red ink.
items.props_detail: The front cover of the official report, marred by a large 'REJECTED' stamp.
items.camera_angle: High angle, looking directly down onto the desk.
items.lighting: Slightly shadowy office lighting from an unseen overhead source.
items.mood: The blunt finality of bureaucratic rejection, a critical warning ignored.
items.narration_anchor: Quince años antes, en mil novecientos noventa y dos, una investigación parlamentaria había recomendado limpiar los relaves. El gobierno rechazó esas recomendaciones.

items.subject: The Wittenoom Gorge landscape, scarred by mining.
items.action: Vast quantities of asbestos tailings spill down the gorge walls like pale blue glaciers, smothering the natural red rock.
items.gaze_interaction: The visual focus is the jarring contrast between the industrial waste and the natural environment.
items.color_palette: The sickly pale blue-grey of the asbestos tailings against the deep reds and ochres of the gorge.
items.props_detail: The sheer volume and spread of the mining waste, covering a huge area.
items.lens_technique: Wide-angle lens with deep depth of field.
items.lighting: Bright, harsh desert sun that bleaches the color from the tailings.
items.mood: A sense of permanent, large-scale environmental violation; a shameful, toxic legacy.
items.narration_anchor: «La minería en los desfiladeros ha dejado una contaminación que solo puede describirse como vergonzosa, incluso para los estándares de la época», dijo Larry Graham.

items.subject: Fine asbestos dust rising from a tailings pile.
items.action: A gust of wind blows across the surface of the asbestos waste, lifting a visible cloud of pale blue fibers into the air.
items.gaze_interaction: The focus is the ethereal, deadly movement of the airborne dust cloud as it begins to disperse.
items.setting: The edge of a massive tailings field in the Australian outback.
items.color_palette: Pale blue-grey dust against a red-earth foreground and a hazy, dusty blue sky.
items.props_detail: The plume of airborne asbestos fibers, made visible by the low sun.
items.lighting: Late afternoon golden hour light, backlighting the dust cloud and making the particles glow.
items.mood: An insidious, unstoppable contamination; a deceptively beautiful but lethal dispersion.
items.narration_anchor: «Tenemos el deber de impedir una mayor dispersión de los relaves de asbesto», dijo Mark Nevill, por los residentes, por los visitantes, por las generaciones futuras.

items.subject: A page from a government financial report.
items.action: The camera focuses on a single line item, 'Wittenoom Site Remediation', followed by a staggering multi-million dollar figure.
items.gaze_interaction: The focus is entirely on the astronomical cost, which is circled in red pen.
items.setting: A document laid out on an office desk, circa 2016.
items.color_palette: Black and white of the printed report, with the red circle drawing the eye.
items.props_detail: A printed spreadsheet or report with columns of figures, highlighting the remediation cost.
items.lens_technique: Macro lens, isolating the single line of text and numbers.
items.lighting: Focused light from a desk lamp, creating a slight glare on the paper.
items.mood: The cold, brutal arithmetic of inaction; a human tragedy reduced to an prohibitive expense.
items.narration_anchor: En dos mil dieciséis, los documentos dicen por qué los relaves siguen donde están: no porque no se pueda, sino por lo que cuesta.

items.subject: A high-resolution digital map on a large monitor.
items.action: A thin layer of real red dust is scattered across the screen's surface, partially obscuring the map where a finger points to the blank space where Wittenoom used to be.
items.gaze_interaction: The finger traces the empty spot on the digital map, while the physical dust defies the erasure.
items.setting: A darkened, modern geological survey office.
items.color_palette: The vibrant satellite colors of the map seen through a film of real, ochre-colored dust.
items.props_detail: A fine coating of actual reddish dust covering the glass of the monitor.
items.camera_angle: Eye-level, angled to catch the screen's glow on the dust particles.
items.lighting: The monitor screen is the sole source of light.
items.mood: Grim irony; the unstoppable physical reality of the dust mocking the futility of digital and bureaucratic erasure.
items.narration_anchor: En dos mil veintitrés, los estudios del Estado sobre hasta dónde llega la contaminación ya estaban desactualizados. Borraron el nombre del mapa. El polvo no leía mapas.
